turns.content: Identify the lowest electronic ionization transition of 12C32S and relate it to the rigid-rotor constant.
Using B=h/(8 pi^2 I) and I=mu r^2, derive r in terms of the observed transition frequency and reduced mass.
Calculate the reduced mass of 12C32S using the stated mass of 34S.
Treat 48991.0 MHz as the rotational constant B rather than the observed transition frequency and convert it to SI units.
Calculate the C-S bond distance and state whether absorption drives an upward or downward rotational transition.
Check the factor of two in nu=2B, the reduced-mass moment of inertia, and the distance scale.
Report the bond distance as a rigid-rotor spectroscopic estimate with nonzero model and measurement uncertainty.
